findings.claim: The policy requires a formal inpatient admission order from a qualified practitioner. The case facts do not show whether such an order exists, who wrote it, or whether it was authenticated, so this eligibility condition is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: The order must specify admission for inpatient services.
findings.case_fact: The appellant billed Medicare for the beneficiary’s inpatient hospitalization from July 27, through July 29, 2005.

findings.claim: Wound care, including pressure sores, is a category of service the policy treats as skilled nursing when a licensed nurse's skills are needed. The pressure-ulcer care here falls within that category, but whether a nurse's skills were actually needed is not settled.
findings.quote: Care of wounds, (including, but not limited to, ulcers, burns, pressure sores, open surgical sites, fistulas, tube sites, and tumor erosion sites)
findings.case_fact: provided wound care, including cleansing and dressing the wound; and instructed the beneficiary’s caregivers in wound care.

findings.claim: Nurse observation and assessment of the sacral pressure ulcer, and teaching caregivers wound care, are the kinds of skilled monitoring and teaching the policy recognizes. This supports the type of service being covered, but not that the other eligibility conditions are met.
findings.quote: the wound may still require skilled monitoring for signs and symptoms of infection or complication (see §40.1.2.1)
findings.case_fact: the provider’s nurses observed and assessed the pressure ulcer on the beneficiary’s sacrum

findings.claim: The policy requires the plan of care to contain specific wound-treatment instructions. The only plan of care described in the case facts covers diabetic assessment, teaching and skin care, with no wound-treatment order. It is UNKNOWN whether this condition is met. The passages also say nothing on patient status or certification, so those points are UNKNOWN too.
findings.quote: the plan of care must contain the specific instructions for the treatment of the wound.
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s plan of care (POC) called for one skilled nursing visit every other week or as needed

findings.claim: Skilled nursing teaching of family or caregivers about the treatment regimen is a covered type of service. The case facts do not show whether the other basic conditions (patient status, certification, physician orders) are met, so that point is UNKNOWN.
findings.quote: skilled nursing personnel to teach a patient, the patient's family, or caregivers how to manage the treatment regimen would constitute skilled nursing services
findings.case_fact: the skilled nursing visits were necessary to teach family members to provide the beneficiary with a proper diet and to encourage fluids

findings.claim: Skilled observation and assessment by a nurse is a covered category of service. Whether these visits meet the policy's conditions is not settled by the facts, so eligibility cannot be confirmed.
findings.quote: skilled observation and assessment by a licensed nurse will result in changes to the treatment of the patient, then the services would be covered
findings.case_fact: required skilled nursing visits for assessment of diabetes, peripheral vascular disease, osteoarthrosis

findings.claim: The policy requires the home health record to document why skilled services are required. The case facts give no homebound status, certification, or orders, and nurse notes suggest a stable, non-symptomatic condition, so eligibility remains unresolved.
findings.quote: The home health record must document the reason skilled services are required and why the nursing visits are reasonable and necessary
findings.case_fact: nurses notes reflect that the beneficiary was not symptomatic and received an oral diabetic agent, rather than injections.

findings.claim: Gait training is a covered type of skilled physical therapy. The notes document skilled gait training at each visit, and the beneficiary has arthritis, a skeletal condition affecting walking.
findings.quote: constitute skilled physical therapy and are considered reasonable and necessary if they can be expected to materially improve
findings.case_fact: The physical therapy visit notes reflect that skilled gait training occurred during each visit.

findings.claim: Physical therapy is a qualifying skilled need for the home health benefit. The beneficiary was admitted to home health with arthritis diagnoses and a physician's order for PT.
findings.quote: including having a need for skilled nursing care on an intermittent basis, physical therapy
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s physician ordered physical therapy once a week for one week, and twice a week for five weeks

findings.claim: The plan of care orders appear specific as to professional, service nature and frequency. The PT order states frequency and purpose.
findings.quote: The orders on the plan of care must indicate the type of services to be provided to the patient
findings.case_fact: The beneficiary’s physician ordered physical therapy once a week for one week, and twice a week for five weeks

findings.claim: A certification and plan of care exist in the record. Whether the supporting physician documentation is sufficient to show eligibility is not settled by the facts (UNKNOWN). Homebound status is also not addressed by the passages (UNKNOWN).
findings.quote: If the documentation used as the basis for the certification of eligibility is not sufficient to demonstrate that the patient is or was eligible
findings.case_fact: Specifically, the “Home Health Certification and Plan of Care” reflects that the beneficiary experienced an exacerbation of arthritis
